chunks: And by his chain, from Hammad, from Hareez, from Zurara who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: God prescribed the salat, and the Messenger of God (blessings of God be upon him and his family) established the Sunnah upon ten aspects: the salat of the resident and the traveler, and the salat of fear in three aspects, and the salat for the eclipse of the sun and the moon, and the salat of the two Eids, and the salat for rain, and the salat over the deceased.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ عَلَى الْمَيِّتِ: Funeral prayer (salat al-janaza); performed over the deceased before burial
key_terms.سَنَّ: Established as Sunnah; the Prophet's normative practice giving specific form to divine obligation
key_terms.صَلَاةَ الِاسْتِسْقَاءِ: Rain prayer (salat al-istisqa); communal supplication for rain during drought
key_terms.صَلَاةَ الْخَوْفِ: Prayer of fear (salat al-khawf); performed during battle or danger in shortened or altered form
key_terms.صَلَاةَ كُسُوفِ: Eclipse prayer; performed at solar or lunar eclipses
key_terms.فَرَضَ: Prescribed as obligatory (fard); a divine command binding on all believers

ai.seo_question: What are the ten types of prayer established by the Prophet Muhammad according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) delineates the ten forms of prayer established by the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) upon the foundational obligation God prescribed. This hadith distinguishes between the divine obligation of salat itself and the Prophetic Sunnah that gave it specific ritual forms. The ten categories include situational prayers (travel, fear, eclipse, rain) alongside scheduled communal and funerary rites, reflecting the comprehensive jurisprudential framework developed by the Imam for his followers.

en.hubeali: And by his chain, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said,

‘Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘Allahazwj Necessitated the Salāt, and Rasool-Allahsaww established the Sunnah upon ten aspects – Salāt of the non-traveller, and the traveller, and the Salāt of fear being upon three aspects, and Salāt of the eclipse of the sun and the moon, and Salāt of the two Eids, and Salāt for the rain, and Salāt upon the deceased’.
en.sarwar: 3. Through the chain of his narrators Hammad has narrated from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “

‘Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Allah has made Salah (prayer) obligatory. The Messenger of Allah has established ten kinds of traditions in Salah (prayer): Salah (prayer) at home and during a journey. Salah (prayer) due to fear is of three kinds. There is Salah (prayer) because of sun eclipse and moon eclipse. There is Salah (prayer) of the two ‘Id. There is Salah (prayer) for rain and (lastly) Salah (prayer) for a deceased.’”
